speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues. To begin, how old are you, and for how long has the swelling been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia.

This 18-month-old boy presents with spontaneous right knee swelling (hemarthrosis) after minor activity, with no trauma reported, alongside a family history of similar issues in his maternal uncle. The clinical picture strongly suggests a hereditary bleeding disorder. Before confirming, I need to verify this with specific lab tests.

REQUEST TEST: PTT (Partial Thromboplastin Time)
REQUEST TEST: PT (Prothrombin Time)
REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII activity level
